title: Why Two Wheels Do Not Fall Over
summary: Tells how the reason a riderless bicycle stays balanced on its own when pushed was long attributed to the gyroscopic effect and to the caster trail of the front wheel, and how the two-mass-skate (TMS) experiment carried out in two thousand eleven showed that these explanations are not necessary, since the bicycle still stayed balanced even though the experiment cancelled both effects. The episode reveals why the self-righting of this everyday machine, whose equations were written in eighteen ninety-nine, has no single-sentence explanation.
